chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Regarding a junub man who performs ghusl, and the water splashes into his vessel, he said:
He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.

key_terms.إِنَائِهِ: his vessel or container holding water
key_terms.الدِّينِ: the religion, meaning the divine law and practice
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water used in the act described
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm or problem in it

ai.seo_question: Does water splashing into the vessel during ghusl for a junub person make it problematic?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that if a junub person performs ghusl and some water splashes back into his vessel, there is no problem in that. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling by citing the Qur'anic principle that Allah has not placed hardship in the religion.
